//: Runway for abs_mu_jump.json (and the legacy config/ice_transition.json
//1: scripted demo): dry asphalt, then ice from x=0 onwards.
//3: The asphalt run-up has to be long enough for the whole PRE-brake half
//4: of the scenario -- reach entry speed AND settle off the throttle --
//5: before the vehicle reaches x=0.  It used to be 40 m spawn-to-boundary,
//6: which is 36 % of that whole budget -- enough for the launch alone and
//7: nothing else -- so the car crossed onto the ice at full throttle and
//8: the mu-jump this level exists for never happened: braking began 34 m
//9: past the boundary, i.e. entirely on ice.  Spawn to boundary is now
//12: Budget, measured with scripts/scenario_runway_report.py on the ramped
//14: launch, 0 -> 15 m/s  43.8 m   (entry speed at t = 7.72 s)
//16: brake on, asphalt     4.9 m   before the boundary
//19: The last line is deliberate and bounded.  Braking starts on asphalt,
//20: but only 4.9 m of it -- 42 % of the 11.6 m a stop from 14.29 m/s
//21: takes at this surface's own friction limit (v^2 / 2*0.9*g) -- so the
//22: car cannot stop before the ice however well ABS performs, and reaches
//23: the boundary at >= 10.9 m/s (24 mph) even in that best case.  What it
//24: actually crossed at, with no BTCM attached: 13.69 m/s (30.6 mph).
//25: Crossing under braking is the point -- this is the transition-braking
//26: test, and the transition belongs INSIDE the brake event.  What it must
//27: not be inside is the launch.
//29: That 4.9 m is the tightest number on this level and it is a DERIVED
//30: one: brake-on position is wherever the car has got to at the brake
//31: event's fixed time, so it moves with launch performance.  A future
//32: change that speeds the launch up by ~4 % puts brake-on past x=0 and
//33: this scenario silently becomes an all-ice stop again.  Re-run
//34: scripts/scenario_runway_report.py after any powertrain or throttle
